questions.prompt: Are you interested in fashion trends?
questions.sampleA1: Yes. I like clothes. New clothes good.
questions.sampleA2: Yes, I like fashion. I like to see new clothes in shops. And I like to buy new t-shirts, but I don't like expensive clothes because they cost too much.
questions.sampleB1: I am interested in fashion trends, but not too much. I like to see what is new in the shops. I think it's important to have nice clothes. For example, when I go to a party, I want to look good. However, I don't want to spend too much money.
questions.sampleB2: To be honest, I'd say I'm only mildly interested in fashion trends. I like to keep up with what's in style, but I don't splash out on designer labels every season. The thing is, I'd rather stick to clothes that suit my personality and feel comfortable than chase every passing fad.
questions.uzSampleA1: Ha. Menga kiyimlar yoqadi. Yangi kiyimlar yaxshi.
questions.uzSampleA2: Ha, menga moda yoqadi. Do'konlarda yangi kiyimlarni ko'rishni yaxshi ko'raman. Va yangi futbolkalar sotib olishni yaxshi ko'raman, lekin qimmat kiyimlarni yoqtirmayman, chunki ular juda qimmat turadi.
questions.uzSampleB1: Men moda tendentsiyalariga qiziqaman, lekin unchalik emas. Menga do'konlarda nima yangi ekanligini ko'rish yoqadi. Menimcha, chiroyli kiyimlarga ega bo'lish muhim. Masalan, men ziyofatga borganimda, yaxshi ko'rinishni xohlayman. Biroq, men juda ko'p pul sarflashni xohlamayman.
questions.uzSampleB2: Men moda tendentsiyalariga qiziqishim bor deb ayta olaman. Men har bir mavsum kolleksiyalarini qat'iy kuzatib boradigan odam emasman, lekin jurnallar va internetni ko'rib, nima dolzarb ekanligini bilish menga yoqadi. Tendentsiyalar kengroq madaniy o'zgarishlarni qanday aks ettirishini kuzatish qiziq. Men zamonaviy kiyimlarni qadrlasam ham, o'tib ketadigan urf-odatlarga ko'r-ko'rona rioya qilishdan ko'ra qulaylik va amaliylikka ustunlik beraman. Oxir-oqibat, men shunchaki so'nggi tendentsiyalarni quvishdan ko'ra, o'zimga xos va abadiy tuyuladigan shaxsiy uslubga intilaman.

vocabulary.title: Q1 - Are you interested in fashion trends?
idioms: dress to impress - "taassurot qoldirish uchun kiyinmoq"
old habits die hard - "eski odatlarni tashlab bo'lmaydi"
clothes make the man - "kiyim odamni yasaydi"
sentenceStarters: "To be honest, I'm moderately interested in…" - "Rostini aytsam, men … ga o'rtacha qiziqaman"
"I wouldn't call myself a fashion enthusiast, but…" - "O'zimni moda ishqibozi deb aytmayman, lekin…"

questions.sampleAnswer:
To be honest, I'm moderately interested in fashion trends. I wouldn't call myself a fashion enthusiast, but I do like to keep up with what's popular and make sure I look presentable.
However, I don't blindly follow every trend — I prefer to stick to styles that suit my personality and body type. I think fashion should be about expressing yourself rather than just copying what's on the runway. As they say, "style is a way to say who you are without having to speak."
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Rostini aytsam, men moda tendentsiyalariga o'rtacha qiziqaman. O'zimni moda ishqibozi deb atay olmayman, lekin mashhur bo'lgan narsalardan xabardor bo'lishni va o'zimni tartibli ko'rsatishni yoqtiraman.

Biroq, men har bir tendentsiyaga ko'r-ko'rona ergashmayman — o'z shaxsiyatimga va tana tuzilishimga mos keladigan uslublarga amal qilishni afzal ko'raman. O'ylashimcha, moda shunchaki podiumda nima bo'layotganini nusxalashdan ko'ra, o'zingni ifoda qilish haqida bo'lishi kerak. Aytishlaricha, "uslub - bu gapirmasdan o'zing kimligingni aytish usuli".

questions.prompt: Did you play any sports as a child?
questions.sampleA1: Yes. I play football. I like it.
questions.sampleA2: Yes, I played football when I was a child. I liked it very much. And I played with my friends in the park.
questions.sampleB1: Yes, I played sports when I was a child. I used to play football and basketball. I think football was my favourite because it was very fun. Also, I played with my friends every day after school. However, I wasn't very good at basketball.
questions.sampleB2: Yes, definitely. Growing up, I was quite the outdoor kid — I played football almost every day after school. To be honest, I wasn't particularly gifted, but I absolutely loved it. Looking back, those matches in the park really taught me about teamwork and how to get along with others. I suppose it brought out the competitive side in me.
questions.uzSampleA2: Ha, men bolaligimda futbol o'ynaganman. Menga juda yoqardi. Va men do'stlarim bilan parkda o'ynardim.
questions.uzSampleB1:
Ha, men bolaligimda sport bilan shug'ullanganman. Men futbol va basketbol o'ynardim. Menimcha, futbol menga eng yoqadigani edi, chunki u juda qiziqarli edi. Shuningdek, men har kuni maktabdan keyin do'stlarim bilan o'ynardim.
Biroq, men basketbolda unchalik yaxshi emasdim.
questions.uzSampleB2: Ha, men bolaligimda sport bilan shug'ullanganman. Men asosan futbol o'ynardim, bu mening mahallamda juda mashhur edi. Biz soatlab parkda to'p tepardik. Men bir muddat suzish darslariga ham qatnashdim, garchi men unda juda yaxshi natijalarga erishdim deb ayta olmasam ham. Menimcha, bu mashg'ulotlarda qatnashish menga ijtimoiy ko'nikmalarni rivojlantirishga va jamoada ishlashni o'rganishga yordam berdi. Bu mening bolaligimning juda muhim qismi edi, aslida.

vocabulary.title: Q2 - Did you play any sports as a child?
idioms: a level playing field - "teng sharoitlar"
get the ball rolling - "ishni boshlamoq"
be on the ball - "ziyrak va tayyor bo'lmoq"
sentenceStarters: "Yes, I definitely did! As a child, I was…" - "Ha, albatta! Bolaligimda men…"
"Looking back, I think those experiences…" - "Orqaga qarab, menimcha o'sha tajribalar…"

questions.sampleAnswer:
Yes, I definitely did! As a child, I was quite active and loved playing football with my friends in the neighbourhood. We used to play almost every evening after school, and it was one of the highlights of my day.
I also tried my hand at swimming and basketball, although I wasn't particularly talented at either. Looking back, I think those experiences helped me develop teamwork skills and taught me the value of fair play. As they say, "it's not whether you win or lose, it's how you play the game."
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Ha, albatta o'ynaganman! Bolaligimda juda faol edim va mahalladagi do'stlarim bilan futbol o'ynashni yaxshi ko'rardim. Maktabdan keyin deyarli har kuni kechqurun o'ynardik va bu kunimning eng yaxshi qismlaridan biri edi.

Men, shuningdek, suzish va basketbolda ham o'zimni sinab ko'rdim, garchi ularning hech birida unchalik iste'dodli bo'lmasam ham. O'ylab qarasam, bu tajribalar menga jamoada ishlash qobiliyatini rivojlantirishga yordam berdi va halol o'yinning qadrini o'rgatdi. Aytishlaricha, "g'alaba qozonish yoki mag'lub bo'lish muhim emas, o'yinni qanday o'ynashing muhim."

questions.prompt: Do you prefer texting or calling?
questions.sampleA1:
I like text.

It is easy.

Call is hard.
questions.sampleA2:
I like texting better.

Because it's quiet and I can read it again.

Calling is okay, but sometimes I'm busy.

So I prefer texting.
questions.sampleB1:
I think I prefer texting to calling.

It's more convenient because I can respond when I have time.

Also, with texting, I have a record of the conversation.

However, if it's something important, I might call.

Calling is faster sometimes.
questions.sampleB2: I suppose it depends on the situation, but on the whole I lean towards texting. The thing is, it's far less intrusive — I can reply at my own convenience without putting someone on the spot. That said, when something's urgent or emotionally charged, I'd rather call, because you can pick up on the person's tone of voice.
questions.uzSampleA1:
Menga xabar yozish yoqadi.

Bu oson.

Qo'ng'iroq qilish qiyin.
questions.uzSampleA2:
Menga xabar yozish ko'proq yoqadi.

Chunki u jim va men uni qayta o'qishim mumkin.

Qo'ng'iroq qilish yaxshi, lekin ba'zan men band bo'laman.

Shuning uchun men xabar yozishni afzal ko'raman.
questions.uzSampleB1:
Menimcha, qo'ng'iroq qilishdan ko'ra xabar yozishni afzal ko'raman.

Bu qulayroq, chunki vaqtim bo'lganda javob bera olaman.

Bundan tashqari, xabar yozish orqali suhbatning yozuvi bo'ladi.

Biroq, agar bu muhim narsa bo'lsa, men qo'ng'iroq qilishim mumkin.

Qo'ng'iroq qilish ba'zan tezroq bo'ladi.
questions.uzSampleB2:
Umuman olganda, men aloqa qilishning afzal usuli sifatida xabar yozishga moyilman.

Bu asinxron aloqaga imkon beradi, ya'ni men darhol javob berishga majbur bo'lmasdan, o'z vaqtimda javob bera olaman.

Bundan tashqari, u yozma yozuvni taqdim etadi, bu esa keyinchalik ma'lumotga murojaat qilish uchun foydali bo'lishi mumkin.

Shunga qaramay, qo'ng'iroq qilishning afzalliklari bor, ayniqsa noziklik va ohang muhim bo'lganda yoki darhol e'tiborni talab qiladigan shoshilinch masalalar bilan shug'ullanganda.

Oxir oqibat, eng yaxshi usul aniq kontekstga va suhbatning mohiyatiga bog'liq.

vocabulary.title: Q3 - Do you prefer texting or calling?
idioms: get the message across - "fikrini yetkazmoq"
on the same page - "bir xil fikrda bo'lmoq"
actions speak louder than words - "amal so'zdan kuchli"
sentenceStarters: "I'd say I generally prefer texting because…" - "Menimcha, men odatda xabar yozishni afzal ko'raman, chunki…"
"When it comes to more urgent matters…" - "Shoshilinch masalalarga kelganda…"

questions.sampleAnswer:
I'd say I generally prefer texting because it gives me time to think about my response and I can reply at my own convenience. It's also less intrusive — I don't have to worry about interrupting someone's day.
However, when it comes to more urgent matters or emotional conversations, I think calling is far more effective. You can hear the person's tone of voice and convey emotions much better. So it really depends on the situation, but for everyday communication, texting is my go-to choice.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Men odatda xabar yozishni afzal ko'raman, chunki bu menga javobim haqida o'ylashga vaqt beradi va men o'zimga qulay vaqtda javob bera olaman. Bundan tashqari, bu kamroq xalaqit beradi — men kimningdir kunini buzishdan xavotirlanmasam ham bo'ladi.

Biroq, shoshilinch masalalar yoki hissiy suhbatlarga kelsak, menimcha, qo'ng'iroq qilish ancha samaraliroq. Siz odamning ovoz ohangini eshitishingiz va his-tuyg'ularni ancha yaxshi ifoda etishingiz mumkin. Shunday qilib, bu haqiqatan ham vaziyatga bog'liq, lekin kundalik aloqa uchun xabar yozish mening asosiy tanlovimdir.

questions.prompt: What do you see in these pictures?
questions.sampleA1: I see kids. They plant tree. Tree is green. I like tree.
questions.sampleA2: I see kids. They are planting trees. In one picture, adults help them. But in the other picture, the kids plant the trees by themselves. It is good.
questions.sampleB1: In the pictures, I can see children planting trees. In one picture, the children are working with adults. The adults are helping them. However, in the other picture, the children are planting trees by themselves. I think it's good for children to learn about nature.
questions.sampleB2: In both pictures, children are planting saplings outdoors, which is lovely to see. In the first one, though, four young kids are getting on with it entirely on their own — crouched around a little tree in the forest, with no grown-ups in sight. The second picture, by contrast, shows adults lending a hand: a woman is kneeling beside a girl, guiding her as she pats down the soil, while other families work away in the sunlit background. So the main difference, I suppose, is independence versus supervision — one shows self-reliance, the other teamwork with grown-ups.
questions.uzSampleA1: Men bolalarni ko'ryapman. Ular daraxt ekishyapti. Daraxt yashil. Menga daraxt yoqadi.
questions.uzSampleA2: Men bolalarni ko'ryapman. Ular daraxt ekishyapti. Bir rasmda kattalar ularga yordam beryapti. Lekin boshqa rasmda bolalar daraxtlarni o'zlari ekishyapti. Bu yaxshi.
questions.uzSampleB1: Rasmlarda bolalarning daraxt ekayotganini ko'rishim mumkin. Bir rasmda bolalar kattalar bilan birga ishlamoqda. Kattalar ularga yordam bermoqda. Biroq, boshqa rasmda bolalar daraxtlarni o'zlari ekmoqda. O'ylashimcha, bolalar tabiat haqida bilib olishlari yaxshi.
questions.uzSampleB2:
Rasmlarda daraxt ekish bilan shug'ullanayotgan bolalar tasvirlangan. Bir rasmda bolalar mustaqil ravishda, kattalarning yordamisiz ishlayotgani aks etgan.
Aksincha, boshqa rasmda bolalar kattalar bilan birga daraxt ekmoqda, ular yo'l-yo'riq va yordam bermoqda. Bu atrof-muhit ta'limiga turli xil yondashuvlarni ifodalashi mumkin, yoki o'ziga ishonishga, yoki tuzilgan o'qishga e'tibor qaratadi.

vocabulary.title: Q4 - What do you see in these pictures?
idioms: a picture is worth a thousand words - "bir rasm ming so'zga arziydi"
learn the ropes - "ishning sir-asrorini o'rganmoq"
practice makes perfect - "mashq mukammallikka olib keladi"
sentenceStarters: "In the first picture, I can see…" - "Birinchi rasmda men ko'ryapman…"
"The contrast between the two images highlights…" - "Ikki rasm orasidagi farq … ni ko'rsatadi"

questions.sampleAnswer:
In the first picture, I can see a group of children planting trees independently, without any adult supervision. They seem to be working together as a team, taking full responsibility for the task and showing a great deal of initiative.
In the second picture, children are planting trees with adults helping and guiding them. The adults appear to be actively involved, showing the children the correct techniques and offering encouragement. The contrast between the two images highlights the difference between independent learning and guided mentorship.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Birinchi rasmda men bir guruh bolalarni hech qanday kattalar nazoratisiz, mustaqil ravishda daraxt ekayotganini ko'rishim mumkin. Ular jamoa bo'lib ishlayotganga o'xshaydi, vazifani to'liq o'z zimmalariga olib, katta tashabbus ko'rsatmoqdalar.

Ikkinchi rasmda bolalar kattalarning yordami va yo'l-yo'riqlari ostida daraxt ekishmoqda. Kattalar faol ishtirok etayotganga o'xshaydi, bolalarga to'g'ri usullarni ko'rsatib, ularni ruhlantirmoqda. Ikkala rasm o'rtasidagi farq mustaqil o'rganish va yo'naltiruvchi murabbiylik o'rtasidagi farqni ta'kidlaydi.

questions.prompt: Why do many children nowadays like working independently?
questions.sampleA1: I think children like work alone. Because it is fun. I like it too.
questions.sampleA2: I think kids like to work alone because they can do it their way. And maybe it is more easy for them. But sometimes they need help from the teacher.
questions.sampleB1: I think many children like working independently because they can choose what to do. Also, it's good for them because they can learn to solve problems by themselves. For example, if they have a difficult task, they can try different ways to find the answer. However, sometimes it's better to work with others.
questions.sampleB2: Well, I suppose there are a couple of reasons. For one thing, modern schools really push for self-directed learning, so kids get used to it early on. On top of that, working alone gives them a real sense of ownership — they can do things their own way and take full credit when it pays off.
questions.uzSampleA1: Menimcha, bolalar yolg'iz ishlashni yoqtirishadi. Chunki bu qiziqarli. Menga ham yoqadi.
questions.uzSampleA2: Menimcha, bolalar yolg'iz ishlashni yoqtirishadi, chunki ular buni o'z usullarida qila olishadi. Va balki bu ular uchun osonroqdir. Lekin ba'zida ularga o'qituvchidan yordam kerak bo'ladi.
questions.uzSampleB1: Menimcha, ko'p bolalar mustaqil ishlashni yoqtirishadi, chunki ular nima qilishni tanlashlari mumkin. Shuningdek, bu ular uchun yaxshi, chunki ular muammolarni o'zlari hal qilishni o'rganishlari mumkin. Masalan, agar ularda qiyin vazifa bo'lsa, ular javobni topish uchun turli usullarni sinab ko'rishlari mumkin. Biroq, ba'zida boshqalar bilan ishlash yaxshiroqdir.
questions.uzSampleB2: Xo'sh, menimcha, hozirgi kunda ko'plab bolalar mustaqil ishlashni bir necha sabablarga ko'ra yoqtirishadi. Birinchidan, ehtimol, ular natijani ko'proq nazorat qilishayotganini his qilishadi va chalg'imasdan diqqatni jamlay olishadi. Bundan tashqari, maktablarda individual yutuqlarga zamonaviy urg'u berilishi ham bu afzallikka hissa qo'shishi mumkin. Ular o'zlari muvaffaqiyatga erishganda, kattaroq yutuq hissini ham sezishlari mumkin. Biroq, bu har doim ham eng yaxshi yondashuv emas, chunki hamkorlik ham qimmatli mahoratdir.

vocabulary.title: Q5 - Why do many children nowadays like working independently?
idioms: stand on one's own two feet - "o'z oyog'ida turmoq"
take the bull by the horns - "ishga dadil kirishmoq"
every child is an artist - "har bir bola — rassom"
sentenceStarters: "There are several reasons why many children today…" - "Bugungi bolalarning ko'pchiligi … ni afzal ko'rishining bir necha sababi bor"
"Working independently allows children to…" - "Mustaqil ishlash bolalarga … imkonini beradi"

questions.sampleAnswer:
There are several reasons why many children today prefer working independently. Firstly, the modern education system increasingly encourages self-directed learning, which helps children develop confidence in their own abilities. When they manage tasks on their own, they feel a strong sense of personal achievement.
Secondly, technology has made it much easier for children to access information and learn new skills without needing constant adult guidance. With the internet and educational apps, children can explore topics at their own pace and in their own way.
Furthermore, working independently allows children to express their creativity freely without worrying about meeting someone else's expectations. It gives them a sense of ownership over their work, which can be incredibly motivating. As the proverb goes, "give a man a fish and you feed him for a day; teach a man to fish and you feed him for a lifetime."
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Bugungi kunda ko'plab bolalar mustaqil ishlashni afzal ko'rishining bir nechta sabablari bor. Birinchidan, zamonaviy ta'lim tizimi tobora ko'proq o'z-o'zini yo'naltiruvchi o'rganishni rag'batlantiradi, bu bolalarga o'z qobiliyatlariga ishonchni rivojlantirishga yordam beradi. Ular vazifalarni o'zlari uddalashganda, shaxsiy yutuq tuyg'usini his qilishadi.

Ikkinchidan, texnologiya bolalarga doimiy kattalar rahbarligisiz ma'lumot olish va yangi ko'nikmalarni o'rganishni ancha osonlashtirdi. Internet va ta'limiy ilovalar yordamida bolalar mavzularni o'z tezligida va o'z uslubida o'rganishlari mumkin.

Bundan tashqari, mustaqil ishlash bolalarga boshqa birovning umidlarini qondirish haqida qayg'urmasdan, o'z ijodkorliklarini erkin ifoda etishga imkon beradi. Bu ularga o'z ishlari ustidan egalik hissini beradi, bu esa juda rag'batlantiruvchi bo'lishi mumkin. Maqolda aytilganidek, "kishiga baliq berib, uni bir kun boqasan; kishiga baliq ovlashni o'rgat, uni bir umr boqasan."

questions.prompt: Why do some children think that work done with adults is of higher quality?
questions.sampleA1:
Adults know more. They are big.

Adults help.
questions.sampleA2: I think kids think adults are better. Because adults are older. They know more things. And they can do more things than kids.
questions.sampleB1: Well, I think some children believe that work with adults is better because adults have more experience. For example, they've done things many times. Also, children often see adults as teachers or experts. So, they trust what adults do. However, sometimes children are wrong and their own work is good too.
questions.sampleB2: To be honest, I think it comes down to trust. Children tend to look up to adults as experts, so they just assume anything a grown-up touches must be top-notch. The thing is, adults usually iron out the mistakes and add a finishing touch, so the end product genuinely does turn out more polished.
questions.uzSampleA1:
Kattalar ko'proq biladi. Ular katta.

Kattalar yordam beradi.
questions.uzSampleA2: Menimcha, bolalar kattalar yaxshiroq deb o'ylashadi. Chunki kattalar kattaroq. Ular ko'proq narsalarni bilishadi. Va ular bolalarga qaraganda ko'proq narsalarni qila olishadi.
questions.uzSampleB1:
Xo'sh, menimcha, ba'zi bolalar kattalar bilan qilingan ish yaxshiroq deb hisoblashadi, chunki kattalarda ko'proq tajriba bor.
Masalan, ular ko'p marta ishlarni bajarishgan. Shuningdek, bolalar ko'pincha kattalarni o'qituvchi yoki mutaxassis sifatida ko'rishadi. Shuning uchun ular kattalar qilgan ishga ishonishadi.
Biroq, ba'zida bolalar adashishadi va o'zlarining ishlari ham yaxshi bo'ladi.
questions.uzSampleB2:
Nima uchun ba'zi bolalar kattalar tomonidan qilingan ish yuqori sifatli deb o'ylashi qiziq. Asosiy omil, ehtimol, kattalarning tajribasi deb hisoblanadi; bolalar ko'pincha yoshni kompetentlik bilan tenglashtiradilar. Ular kattalar o'z tajribasi va rivojlangan ko'nikmalari tufayli yuqori sifatli ish ishlab chiqaradi deb taxmin qilishlari mumkin.

Bundan tashqari, ko'pincha hokimiyat elementi mavjud. Bolalar kattalarning boshqaruvda bo'lishiga va yo'l-yo'riq berishiga odatlangan, shuning uchun ular bu dinamikani hamkorlikdagi loyihalarga ongsiz ravishda o'tkazishlari, kattalarning hissasi ishni yuqori darajaga ko'taradi deb taxmin qilishlari mumkin. Agar kattalar doimiy ravishda yetakchilik qilsalar yoki bolalarning xatolarini tuzatsalar, bu sifat ierarxiyasini beixtiyor yaratib, bu tushunchani kuchaytirishi mumkin.

vocabulary.title: Q6 - Why do some children think that work done with adults is of higher quality?
idioms: two heads are better than one - "ikki bosh bir boshdan yaxshi"
experience is the best teacher - "tajriba — eng yaxshi o'qituvchi"
you can't teach an old dog new tricks - "keksayganlarni o'rgatish qiyin"
sentenceStarters: "There are a number of reasons why some children believe…" - "Ba'zi bolalarning … deb hisoblashining bir necha sababi bor"
"Children often look up to adults as…" - "Bolalar ko'pincha kattalarni … sifatida hurmat qiladi"

questions.sampleAnswer:
There are a number of reasons why some children believe that work done with adults is of higher quality. Primarily, adults bring years of experience and knowledge that children simply haven't had the chance to acquire yet. When an adult guides a child through a task, they can point out mistakes, suggest better approaches, and ensure that the final result meets a higher standard.
Additionally, children often look up to adults as role models and authority figures, so they naturally trust that adult involvement leads to better outcomes. There's also a psychological element — children may feel more confident about their work when an adult has validated their efforts and provided reassurance.
Moreover, collaborative work with adults tends to be more structured and organised, as adults bring planning skills and attention to detail that young children are still developing. This structure often results in a more polished and well-executed piece of work.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Ba'zi bolalar kattalar bilan qilingan ish yuqori sifatli deb hisoblashining bir qancha sabablari bor. Birinchi navbatda, kattalar ko'p yillik tajriba va bilimlarga ega bo'lib, bolalar ularni hali o'zlashtirishga ulgurmagan. Katta yoshdagi odam bolani vazifani bajarishda yo'naltirsa, ular xatolarni ko'rsatishi, yaxshiroq yondashuvlarni taklif qilishi va yakuniy natija yuqori standartga javob berishini ta'minlashi mumkin.

Bundan tashqari, bolalar ko'pincha kattalarga namuna va obro'li shaxs sifatida qarashadi, shuning uchun ular kattalarning ishtiroki yaxshiroq natijalarga olib kelishiga ishonishadi. Shuningdek, psixologik element ham bor - bolalar kattalar ularning harakatlarini tasdiqlagan va ishonch berganida, o'z ishlariga ko'proq ishonishlari mumkin.

Bundan tashqari, kattalar bilan hamkorlikdagi ishlar ko'proq tuzilgan va tashkil etilgan bo'ladi, chunki kattalar rejalashtirish qobiliyatlari va mayda narsalarga e'tibor berishni olib keladi, bularni yosh bolalar hali rivojlantirmoqda. Ushbu tuzilma ko'pincha yanada mukammal va yaxshi bajarilgan ishga olib keladi.

questions.sampleB2: I'd like to tell you about a time when nature really bowled me over, and that was a couple of summers ago when my family and I went camping up in the mountains. Honestly, I wasn't expecting much, but early one morning I woke up before everyone else and climbed a nearby hill to watch the sunrise. The breathtaking scenery — golden light spilling over the valley, birdsong everywhere, and this incredible stillness — completely took my breath away. I just stood there, soaking it all in. It's a moment I'll never forget. As for how it affected me, I'd say it had a profoundly calming effect. All the stress and little worries I'd been carrying around seemed to melt away in an instant. To be honest, it gave me a real sense of perspective — it reminded me that, in the grand scheme of things, most of my everyday problems are pretty trivial. I came back down that hill feeling refreshed and, oddly enough, much more grateful. The thing is, I genuinely believe spending time in nature can do wonders for your personal development. For one thing, it teaches you patience and mindfulness — you learn to slow down and stop and smell the roses. On top of that, being outdoors clears your head, sparks creativity, and honestly, it does you the world of good physically too. So I suppose my takeaway is that we should all step outside and reconnect with nature far more often than we do, even if it's just a stroll in the local park.

bulletPoints: Share a time when nature inspired you.
How did being in nature affect your thoughts or feelings?
How can spending time in nature benefit personal development?
questions.sampleAnswer:
A time when nature inspired me:
I'd like to share an experience from a couple of years ago when I visited a mountain retreat with my family during the summer holidays. We hiked to the top of a hill early in the morning and watched the sunrise over the valley below. The breathtaking scenery — the golden light, the fresh mountain air, and the complete silence — left me feeling profoundly moved. It was one of those rare moments where everything felt perfectly peaceful.
How being in nature affected my thoughts or feelings:
Being surrounded by nature had a remarkably calming effect on my mind. All the stress and worries I'd been carrying seemed to melt away in that moment. I felt a deep sense of gratitude and clarity — it reminded me that the most important things in life are often the simplest ones. Nature has this unique ability to put things into perspective and help you see the bigger picture.
How spending time in nature can benefit personal development:
I firmly believe that spending time in nature can significantly benefit personal development. It teaches patience, mindfulness, and appreciation for the world around us. Being outdoors encourages physical activity, reduces anxiety, and boosts creativity. As the famous quote goes, "in every walk with nature, one receives far more than he seeks." Nature is, without a doubt, one of the best teachers we have.

Tabiat meni ilhomlantirgan vaqt:

Bir necha yil oldin, yozgi ta'tilda oilam bilan tog' dam olish maskaniga borganimda yuz bergan voqeani aytib bermoqchiman. Biz erta tongda tepalikning eng yuqori qismiga piyoda bordik va quyoshning pastdagi vodiy ustidan chiqishini tomosha qildik. Ajoyib manzara — oltin nur, toza tog' havosi va mutlaq sukunat — meni juda hayajonga soldi. Bu hamma narsa mukammal darajada tinch bo'lgan noyob lahzalardan biri edi.

Tabiatda bo'lish mening fikrlarimga yoki his-tuyg'ularimga qanday ta'sir qildi:

Tabiat bilan o'ralgan bo'lish mening ongimga juda tinchlantiruvchi ta'sir ko'rsatdi. Men olib yurgan barcha stress va tashvishlar o'sha lahzada yo'qolgandek bo'ldi. Men minnatdorchilik va aniqlikni his qildim — bu menga hayotdagi eng muhim narsalar ko'pincha eng oddiy narsalar ekanligini eslatdi. Tabiat narsalarni to'g'ri nuqtai nazarga qo'yish va katta rasmni ko'rishga yordam berishning o'ziga xos qobiliyatiga ega.

Tabiatda vaqt o'tkazish shaxsiy rivojlanishga qanday foyda keltirishi mumkin:

Men tabiatda vaqt o'tkazish shaxsiy rivojlanishga sezilarli darajada foyda keltirishiga qat'iy ishonaman. Bu bizga sabr-toqat, onglilik va atrofimizdagi olamni qadrlashni o'rgatadi. Ochiq havoda bo'lish jismoniy faollikni rag'batlantiradi, xavotirlikni kamaytiradi va ijodkorlikni oshiradi. Mashhur maqolda aytilganidek, "tabiat bilan har bir sayrda inson o'zi izlaganidan ko'ra ko'proq narsaga ega bo'ladi". Tabiat, shubhasiz, bizning eng yaxshi o'qituvchilarimizdan biridir.

questions.prompt: Students should use dormitories at their place of study.
questions.sampleA1: Yes, I like dorm. Dorm is good. Near school. I have friends.
questions.sampleA2: I think dorms are good. It's near the school, and I can walk. It's easy. But sometimes it's noisy, and I don't like that. I like my friends in the dorm.
questions.sampleB1: I think students should live in dorms. It's good because it's close to the university, so you don't have to travel far. Also, you can meet new people and make friends. However, sometimes it can be noisy and difficult to study. But overall, I think it's a good experience.
questions.sampleB2: This is a topic that divides opinion, and I can honestly see merit on both sides. Supporters of dormitory life would argue that it's a fantastic way for students to settle into university. For one thing, living side by side with your peers helps you build social connections and make friends who'll last a lifetime. On top of that, dorms are usually far cheaper than renting a flat, which makes higher education much more financially accessible for students on a tight budget. Being a stone's throw from campus also cuts out that tiring daily commute, which is a real bonus when you've got early lectures. That said, the critics do raise some valid points. The thing is, shared rooms can be noisy and there's often very little privacy, which can really get in the way of studying. On top of that, strict rules like curfews may feel a bit stifling for young adults who are trying to stand on their own two feet. And let's be honest, some dormitories are poorly maintained, with cramped rooms and run-down facilities. Personally, though, I'd come down in favour of dormitories, at least for first-year students. In my view, the sense of community and the money you save far outweigh the drawbacks — provided the university keeps them up to scratch. At the end of the day, a lot depends on the individual, but as the saying goes, home is where you make it. With the right attitude, a dorm can quickly start to feel like a second home.

Shuningdek, siz yangi odamlar bilan tanishishingiz va do'stlar orttirishingiz mumkin. Biroq, ba'zida u shovqinli bo'lishi va o'qish qiyin bo'lishi mumkin. Lekin umuman olganda, menimcha, bu yaxshi tajriba.
questions.uzSampleB2: Talabalar yotoqxonalarda yashashi kerakmi, degan savol qiziqarli. Bir tomondan, yotoqxonada yashash qulay joylashuvni va boshqa talabalar bilan oson muloqot qilish imkoniyatini beradi. Bu, ayniqsa, universitet hayotiga moslashayotgan yangi talabalar uchun foydali bo'lishi mumkin. Boshqa tomondan, yotoqxonalar juda shovqinli bo'lishi va shaxsiy hayotga ega bo'lmasligi mumkin, bu esa o'qish uchun muammo bo'lishi mumkin. Bu haqiqatan ham har bir talabaning ehtiyojlari va xohishlariga bog'liq. Menimcha, universitetlar yotoqxonalarning yaxshi saqlanishini va tinch o'qish joylarini ta'minlashi kerak.

questions.sampleAnswer:
This is a widely debated topic among students and educators alike. Supporters of dormitory living argue that it significantly helps students build social connections and make lifelong friends. Living alongside peers who share similar goals creates a supportive community that can enhance both academic performance and personal growth.
Moreover, dormitories are considerably cheaper than renting private flats, which makes higher education more financially accessible for students from modest backgrounds. The proximity to campus also saves valuable commuting time, allowing students to dedicate more hours to their studies and extracurricular activities.
However, critics raise some valid concerns. Shared living spaces often come with noise and a lack of privacy, which can seriously disrupt concentration and academic work. Additionally, dormitory rules — such as curfews and visitor restrictions — may feel overly controlling for young adults who are trying to develop their independence. There's also the issue of substandard facilities in some institutions, where rooms are cramped and amenities are poorly maintained.
Personally, I believe dormitories can be a wonderful experience if they are well-managed and offer a reasonable balance between community living and personal space. As the saying goes, "home is where you make it" — with the right attitude, a dormitory can become a second home.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Bu talabalar va o'qituvchilar orasida keng muhokama qilinadigan mavzu. Yotoqxonalarda yashash tarafdorlari bu talabalarga ijtimoiy aloqalarni o'rnatishga va umrbod do'stlar orttirishga sezilarli yordam beradi, deb ta'kidlaydilar. O'xshash maqsadlarga ega tengdoshlar bilan birga yashash, o'quv faoliyati va shaxsiy o'sishni yaxshilaydigan qo'llab-quvvatlovchi jamiyatni yaratadi.

Bundan tashqari, yotoqxonalar xususiy kvartiralarni ijaraga olishdan ancha arzon, bu esa oliy ma'lumotni kamtarona oilalardan chiqqan talabalar uchun moliyaviy jihatdan yanada ochiq qiladi. Kampusga yaqinlik qimmatli qatnov vaqtini ham tejaydi, bu talabalarga o'qish va sinfdan tashqari mashg'ulotlarga ko'proq vaqt ajratish imkonini beradi.

Biroq, tanqidchilar ba'zi asosli xavotirlarni o'rtaga tashlashadi. Umumiy yashash joylari ko'pincha shovqin va shaxsiy hayotning yo'qligi bilan birga keladi, bu esa diqqatni jamlash va o'quv ishlariga jiddiy xalaqit berishi mumkin. Bundan tashqari, yotoqxona qoidalari - masalan, komendantlik soati va tashrif buyuruvchilarga cheklovlar - mustaqillikni rivojlantirishga harakat qilayotgan yosh kattalar uchun haddan tashqari nazoratdek tuyulishi mumkin. Ba'zi muassasalarda xonalarning torligi va qulayliklarning yomon saqlanishi kabi sifatsiz sharoitlar muammosi ham mavjud.

Shaxsan men, agar yotoqxonalar yaxshi boshqarilsa va jamoaviy hayot bilan shaxsiy makon o'rtasida oqilona muvozanatni taklif qilsa, ajoyib tajriba bo'lishi mumkinligiga ishonaman. Aytishlaricha, "uy - siz uni qayerda qursangiz, o'sha yerda" - to'g'ri munosabat bilan yotoqxona ikkinchi uyga aylanishi mumkin.
